To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genetic factors underlying the locomotor response to ethanol are pleiotropic and are also associated with the locomotor response of mice to cocaine, morphine and nicotine.

1) the genetic influence on locomotion is pleiotropic, 2) the genetic influence in locomotion is mediated by the GABAergic system, and 3) the genetic influence is mediated by GABAergic system through the interaction of genes that are located at different chromosomes.

(a) a reverse selection procedure for differential response to ethanol (EtOH) provides evidence for pleotropic genetic influence on locomotion to other drugs of interest, (b) a reverse selection program for differential response to cocaine (COC) and amphetamine (AMPH) provides evidence for genetic influence on EtOH response, and (c) genetic influence is pleiotropic for EtOH and other drugs of abuse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of differential responses to drugs of abuse.
identifying the genetic and environmental factors that influence the development of drug abuse.
the genetic basis for individual differences in response to drugs of abuse, including the effects of genetic background on response to ethanol and other drugs.
